blocks.heading: A greasy, itchy, flaky scalp even after washing
quotes: “I use hairspray every day and one wash never feels clean.”
“I wash at night and by morning my scalp is greasy.”
“My scalp itches and I scratch off small white flakes.”

explainer.heading: Regular washing does not lift all the dead skin and product residue
body: Excess oil, sweat, hairspray and shampoo residue build up into a film on the scalp. The scalp turns greasy again quickly and itches more easily.

The scrub contains salt grains and is massaged into the wet scalp before washing to lift that film. The description on the tube reads: helps exfoliate the scalp and remove dandruff, excess sebum and impurities, leaving the scalp clean, refreshed and less greasy.

blocks.heading: Who it suits, who should not use it

items.heading: A scalp that gets greasy fast, with hairspray build-up
items.body: Use before washing to lift the film, then shampoo as usual.

items.heading: Small, dry flakes
items.body: Gentle massage helps lift clinging flakes. Thick, patchy flakes or a very red, itchy scalp should be seen by a doctor.

items.heading: A thin, easily sensitised scalp
items.body: Massage very gently and use it less often. Stop if it stings.

items.heading: A scratched or irritated scalp
items.body: The brand says not to use it in this case. Salt grains would make damaged skin sting more.

blocks.heading: Key ingredients
blocks.intro: The first three names are printed on the front of the tube. Glycerin and vitamin E are in the full ingredient list published by the seller.
blocks.caption: The full list published by the seller also includes sodium laureth sulfate (a foaming agent), fragrance and colourants. No concentrations are printed. Check the INCI list on the packaging if you react easily.

rows.name: Sodium Chloride (salt)
rows.role: Salt grains give light friction during massage, helping lift dead skin and excess oil.

rows.name: Gluconobacter/Honey Ferment Filtrate (fermented honey)
rows.role: A honey ferment that helps loosen old surface cells gently.

rows.name: Zingiber Officinale Root Oil (ginger root oil)
rows.role: Gives a light warming, pleasant feel during massage.
rows.suitedFor: People who like a warm feel

rows.name: Glycerin
rows.role: Humectant; keeps the scalp from feeling tight after cleansing.

blocks.heading: How to use it
blocks.intro: Following the brand's shop directions. The front of the tube carries no directions.

items.heading: Apply to the scalp
items.body: Take about 1–2 teaspoons and spread it over the scalp; no need to apply it to the lengths.

items.heading: Massage gently for 3–5 minutes
items.body: Use the fingertips in small circles. Do not scrub hard or use your nails.

items.heading: Rinse, then shampoo as usual
items.body: Rinse out all the salt, then wash with your usual shampoo.

blocks.footnote: Frequency suggested by the brand: once or twice a week. Avoid contact with the eyes.

items.a: The brand suggests once or twice a week. The front of the tube does not state a frequency. With a sensitive scalp, start with once a week.
Before. Massage into the wet scalp, rinse, then shampoo as usual.

items.q: Is it suitable if I have dandruff?
items.a: It lifts flakes clinging to the scalp during massage. Thick, patchy flakes or a very red, itchy scalp are a matter for a dermatologist.
Close the cap after use, keep in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight and out of reach of children.
